content.text:
The solar capture price in October 2026 (1–31 Oct, German local time) was **13.45 ct/kWh (134.49 EUR/MWh)**, calculated from public solar generation weighted against day-ahead prices. The small gap is expected: the official value uses the TSOs' extrapolated feed-in, while this calculation uses Energy-Charts' generation data.

input.b_label: solar share of public net generation, 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08

content.text:
Wind's share was about **3.0 times** solar's in Germany's public net generation from Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026 (23.3% vs 7.75%; ratio 3.006, a difference of 15.55 percentage points).

A correction to my previous answer: I gave the "about 3.0" ratio and the "one-third" comparison without calling the comparison tool. The figure above comes from the tool, so use this one. The "one-third" wording was also imprecise: 7.75% is about one-third of 23.3%, but I should have stated the ratio directly.

wind_speed_last_week.question: How windy was it in Germany last week?

content.text:
Last week (Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026) was calm overall. The mean wind speed across 65 DWD stations was 3.34 m/s, and the highest hourly mean was 5.64 m/s on 4 November at 13:00. Only 12 of 168 hours (7.1%) exceeded 5 m/s, and the windiest day was Wednesday 4 November (daily mean 4.78 m/s). Station wind is measured about 10 m above ground, so it indicates how windy it was rather than what the turbines received at hub height.

Source: Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD), 65 stations (via GridAgent weather data)

price_calm_vs_windy_october.question: In October 2026, how did the day-ahead price in hours with little wind compare with windy hours?

input.a_label: mean day-ahead price, wind below 3 m/s, Oct 2026
input.b_label: mean day-ahead price, wind above 5 m/s, Oct 2026

content.text:
In October 2026 (1–31 October, German local time), the day-ahead price averaged 214.84 EUR/MWh in hours with little wind (station wind below 3 m/s, 304 hours) and 62.61 EUR/MWh in windy hours (above 5 m/s, 144 hours). That is a difference of 152.23 EUR/MWh, a ratio of 3.43.

These are associations, not causal effects; demand, gas prices and imports also shape prices. Wind is the mean of 65 DWD stations at about 10 m height, an indicator of how windy it was, not the wind at turbine hub height. The thresholds (below 3 m/s and above 5 m/s) are my assumptions, not official definitions. The 745 hours cover the full month.

Source: Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de via Energy-Charts.info (day-ahead prices); Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) open data (wind speed)

dunkelflaute_hours_october.question: How many hours in October 2026 had neither wind nor sun?

content.text:
In October 2026, 209 hours (28.1% of the 745 hours in the month) had wind below 3 m/s and solar radiation below 50 W/m². These thresholds are my assumptions, not official definitions. The wind figure is a station indicator from 65 DWD stations at about 10 m height, not hub-height wind. The 745 hours include the extra hour from the autumn clock change.

Source: Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD), via get_weather (CC BY 4.0)

followup_gas_in_dunkelflaute.question: How much power did gas plants produce on average in those hours?

content.text:
In October 2026, 209 of 745 hours had neither wind nor sun, about 28.1% of hours. I used wind speed below 3 m/s and global horizontal irradiance below 50 W/m², both my assumptions rather than official definitions. Wind is the mean of 65 DWD stations at about 10 m height, so it indicates how windy it was rather than what turbines received. The 745 hours include the extra hour of the 25 October clock change, in Berlin time.

Source: Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD), 65 stations, via opendata.dwd.de (CC BY 4.0)

In the 209 hours of October 2026 with wind below 3 m/s and solar radiation below 50 W/m², gas plants produced on average 9,310 MW (about 9.3 GW) of public net generation. Those thresholds are my assumptions, and the hours are hourly weather means matched to the 15-minute generation values.

Source: Energy-Charts.info (Fraunhofer ISE) for generation; Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) via opendata.dwd.de for weather (CC BY 4.0)
